interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 58.43 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 43.82–73.04 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a negative surgical margin, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis. The surgical pathology reported a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pT2c stage. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 5.9. The absence of a biopsy grade comparison to the prostatectomy specimen introduces uncertainty regarding the true tumor biology. Missing postoperative PSA and follow-up data significantly widen the uncertainty surrounding the trajectory of the disease. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent changes would be crucial in refining this prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 58.4 months without an observed event.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2c, negative surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion or lymph node metastasis documented. Preoperative PSA was 5.9. The surgical findings, including "no lymph node metastasis," are favorable prognostic factors. The preoperative PSA level is a factor, though its postoperative trajectory is unknown due to missing follow-up data. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing. The nodal status is documented as no lymph node metastasis. The prognosis is guided by the favorable surgical findings, but the uncertainty is widened by the missing previous notes, which obscure the postoperative PSA trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would significantly revise the prognosis. The current heuristic horizon for recurrence is 58.4 months.
